# Flip Square Submatrix Vertically.

@example The block covers rows 1 to 3 and columns 2 to 4. Rows 1 and 3 trade those three numbers; row 2 is the middle row and stays, as does everything outside the block.
[[11,12,13,14,15],[21,22,23,24,25],[31,32,33,34,35],[41,42,43,44,45]]
1
2
3
=> [[11,12,13,14,15],[21,22,43,44,45],[31,32,33,34,35],[41,42,23,24,25]]

@example A 2 by 2 block in the bottom-left corner; the last column is outside it.
[[5,6,7],[8,9,10],[40,50,60],[70,80,90]]
2
0
2
=> [[5,6,7],[8,9,10],[70,80,60],[40,50,90]]

@example A block of a single tile has nothing to swap with.
[[42,17]]
0
1
1
=> [[42,17]]

# The smallest grid.
[[1]]

1
=> [[1]]

# A single column and a single row: k can only be 1.
[[3],[1],[2]]
1
0
1
=> [[3],[1],[2]]

[[100,1,100]]
0
2
1
=> [[100,1,100]]

# The block is the whole grid.
[[9,1,4],[2,8,6],[7,3,5]]
0
0
3
=> [[7,3,5],[2,8,6],[9,1,4]]

# Even k: every row of the block moves. Column 0 is outside the block, so
# swapping whole rows would be wrong.
[[10,71,72,73,74],[20,81,82,83,84],[30,91,92,93,94],[40,99,98,97,96]]
0
1
4
=> [[10,99,98,97,96],[20,91,92,93,94],[30,81,82,83,84],[40,71,72,73,74]]

# x is a row and y a column: on 2 x 5 and 5 x 3 grids, swapping their

2
=> [[8,9,4,1,6],[2,3,5,7,10]]
